entries.title: I Corinthians 13:1
segments: Though I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have no love, I am become a clanging brass, or a clashing cymbal.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:2
segments: Though I have the gift of prophecy and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:3
segments: And though I sell all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it avails me nothing.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:4
segments: Love suffers long and is kind; love envies not; love makes no parade, is not puffed up,

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:5
segments: is not rude, nor selfish, nor easily provoked. Love bears no malice, never rejoices over wrong-doing,

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:6
segments: but rejoices when the truth rejoices.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:7
segments: It knows how to be silent, it is trustful, hopeful, patient, enduring.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:8
segments: Love never fails; but though there are prophecies, they will fail; though there are tongues, they will cease; though there is knowledge, it will be superseded.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:9
segments: For our knowing is imperfect, and our prophesying is imperfect;

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:10
segments: but when the perfect is come, then the perfect will be done away.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:11
segments: When I was a child I spoke like a child, felt like a child, thought like a child; now that I am become a man, I have done with childish things.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:12
segments: For now we see as in a mirror, and are baffled, but then face to face; now I know in fragments, but then shall I understand even as I also have been understood.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:13
segments: Faith, Hope, Love endure--these three; but the greatest of these is Love.
